messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

You will be given a piece of text and a list of relational triples in the format of [Subject, Relation, Object] extracted from the text. For each relation present in the triples, your task is to write a description to express the meaning of the relation.

Here are some examples:
Example 1:
Text: Lipitor (atorvastatin) belongs to a group of drugs called statins. Lipitor is used together with diet to lower blood levels of "bad" cholesterol (LDL) and to reduce the risk of stroke and heart attack.
Triples: [["Lipitor", "has generic name", "atorvastatin"], ["Lipitor", "belongs to drug class", "statins"], ["Lipitor", "treats", "high LDL cholesterol"], ["Lipitor", "reduces risk of", "stroke"]]
Relations: ["has generic name", "belongs to drug class", "treats", "reduces risk of"]
Answer:
has generic name: The subject drug is known by the generic (non-proprietary) name specified by the object entity.
belongs to drug class: The subject drug is a member of the pharmacological drug class specified by the object entity.
treats: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the medical condition specified by the object entity.
reduces risk of: The subject drug is used to lower the risk of the medical event or condition specified by the object entity.

Example 2:
Text: You should not use metformin if you have severe kidney disease. Tell your doctor if you have ever had liver disease. Metformin may cause lactic acidosis, a serious condition. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking metformin.
Triples: [["metformin", "contraindicated in", "severe kidney disease"], ["metformin", "use with caution in", "liver disease"], ["metformin", "has serious side effect", "lactic acidosis"], ["metformin", "should be avoided with", "alcohol"]]
Relations: ["contraindicated in", "use with caution in", "has serious side effect", "should be avoided with"]
Answer:
contraindicated in: The subject drug should not be used by patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
use with caution in: The subject drug may be unsafe or require medical supervision for patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
has serious side effect: The subject drug may cause the serious or dangerous adverse effect specified by the object entity.
should be avoided with: Patients taking the subject drug should avoid the substance or activity specified by the object entity.

Example 3:
Text: Amlodipine is available as oral tablets in strengths of 2.5 mg, 5 mg, and 10 mg. Overdose symptoms may include rapid heartbeats and fainting. Norvasc is made by Pfizer.
Triples: [["amlodipine", "has dosage form", "oral tablet"], ["amlodipine", "has strength", "2.5 mg"], ["amlodipine", "has overdose symptom", "fainting"], ["Norvasc", "manufactured by", "Pfizer"]]
Relations: ["has dosage form", "has strength", "has overdose symptom", "manufactured by"]
Answer:
has dosage form: The subject drug is available in the pharmaceutical dosage form specified by the object entity.
has strength: The subject drug is available in the dose strength specified by the object entity.
has overdose symptom: An overdose of the subject drug may cause the symptom specified by the object entity.
manufactured by: The subject drug is manufactured or marketed by the company specified by the object entity.

Now please write relation descriptions given the following text and triples. Note that the description needs to be general and can be used to describe relations between other entities as well. Pay attention to the order of subject and object entities. Write exactly one line per relation in the form "relation: description" and nothing else.
Text: Metoprolol is a beta-blocker medication.
Metoprolol is used to treat high blood pressure.
Metoprolol is used to treat chest pain (angina).
Metoprolol is used to treat heart failure.
Metoprolol is used to improve survival after a heart attack.
Metoprolol works mainly on the heart.
Metoprolol is called a cardioselective beta-blocker.
Metoprolol works by blocking the effect of adrenaline and noradrenaline on beta-1 receptors in your heart.
This slows your heart rate.
It reduces how hard your heart squeezes.
It lowers your blood pressure.
Because the heart is doing less work, Metoprolol needs less oxygen.
This is why metoprolol also helps with angina.
Exactly how metoprolol works is not fully understood.
It works for high blood pressure.
It works for heart failure.
It works after a heart attack.
At higher blood levels, metoprolol also blocks beta-2 receptors in the airways and blood vessels.
Metoprolol still needs care in people with breathing problems.
This is because metoprolol blocks beta-2 receptors in the airways and blood vessels at higher blood levels.
Triples: [["Metoprolol", "has drug class", "beta-blocker"], ["Metoprolol", "treats", "high blood pressure"], ["Metoprolol", "treats", "chest pain"], ["Metoprolol", "treats", "heart failure"], ["Metoprolol", "improves survival after", "heart attack"], ["Metoprolol", "acts mainly on", "heart"], ["Metoprolol", "has alternative name", "cardioselective beta-blocker"], ["Metoprolol", "has mechanism of action", "blocking effect of adrenaline and noradrenaline on beta-1 receptors in heart"], ["Metoprolol", "reduces", "heart rate"], ["Metoprolol", "reduces", "heart squeezing force"], ["Metoprolol", "lowers", "blood pressure"], ["Metoprolol", "reduces oxygen demand of", "heart"], ["Metoprolol", "helps with", "angina"], ["Metoprolol", "has mechanism of action", "not fully understood"], ["Metoprolol", "works for", "high blood pressure"], ["Metoprolol", "works for", "heart failure"], ["Metoprolol", "works after", "heart attack"], ["Metoprolol", "blocks", "beta-2 receptors in airways and blood vessels at higher blood levels"], ["Metoprolol", "requires caution in", "people with breathing problems"]]
Relations: ["acts mainly on", "blocks", "has alternative name", "has drug class", "has mechanism of action", "helps with", "improves survival after", "lowers", "reduces", "reduces oxygen demand of", "requires caution in", "treats", "works after", "works for"]
Answer:

completion:
acts mainly on: The subject drug primarily exerts its effects on the anatomical or physiological entity specified by the object entity.  
blocks: The subject drug inhibits or prevents the function of the biological target specified by the object entity.  
has alternative name: The subject drug is also known by the alternative name specified by the object entity.  
has drug class: The subject drug is a member of the pharmacological drug class specified by the object entity.  
has mechanism of action: The subject drug functions through the biological mechanism specified by the object entity.  
helps with: The subject drug provides therapeutic benefit or relief for the condition specified by the object entity.  
improves survival after: The subject drug enhances the chances of survival following the medical event specified by the object entity.  
lowers: The subject drug decreases the level or intensity of the physiological parameter specified by the object entity.  
reduces: The subject drug decreases the level or intensity of the physiological parameter or process specified by the object entity.  
reduces oxygen demand of: The subject drug decreases the amount of oxygen required by the anatomical or physiological entity specified by the object entity.  
requires caution in: The subject drug may require special monitoring or care in patients with the condition specified by the object entity.  
treats: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the medical condition specified by the object entity.  
works after: The subject drug provides therapeutic benefit following the medical event specified by the object entity.  
works for: The subject drug is effective in treating or managing the medical condition specified by the object entity.
